summary: Flathead NF 30-foot L-4 lookout tower about five miles east of Hungry Horse, dated 1932; listed as gone in 1948. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone in 1948, per firelookout.com.

events.note: June 1933 Flathead Courier item: eleven miles of road to be built to two lookout stations, one on Emory hill and one on Desert mountain.
Listed as 'Gone 1948' on firelookout.com; the source does not say how the tower was removed.

evidence.supports: Site lies about five miles east of Hungry Horse in the Flathead National Forest.
June 1933 road plan to two lookout stations, one on Emory hill and one on Desert mountain.
evidence.quote: The larger part of the crew is working at completing a mile and a half of the desert mountain road, clearing and grading. Eleven miles of road are to be built to two lookout stations, on Desert mountain and Emory hill.

evidence.supports: Item predicts the road crew's work would help safeguard timber in the Coram Experimental Forest.
evidence.quote: The crew's work will be successful in protecting vast bodies of green timber in the Coram experimental forest.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association's Montana list marks the tower as gone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Only firelookout.com dates the tower (1932). The 1933 newspaper item describes road plans for lookout stations and does not confirm a build date.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: three sources, no description of the site today, and no staffing history. The 1948 date comes only from firelookout.com and the reason for removal is not given. The Hungry Horse News 1948 archive (loc.gov) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. A Flathead NF history (npshistory.com, chapter 6) does not mention Emery Hill. Firelookout.com spells the name Emery; the 1933 item spells it Emory. Worth checking Hungry Horse News 1948 and Flathead NF lookout records before publication.
